sections.name: Home
sections.shared: Home is the workbench, not a statistics page: it shows what needs doing now. A section chooser summarises each section's workload; a section's Overview groups work by task type with timing and progress; picking a unit narrows the counts. Scan and Toolbox stay in reach, and the Assistant opens from the header.

features.prd:
# Environment & devices 环境与设备

## Problem

A worker in a unit needs to see whether the room is right (temperature, humidity, ammonia), to set the ventilation fan, and to report and close equipment faults, without leaving the unit. The old UI has no such place; faults and sensors were scattered across Inspection.

## Who

Floor workers and supervisors responsible for a unit.

## Anchor

None. Two groups: Sensors and devices; Maintenance. The only lifecycle is an issue: open, then resolved.

## Rules

- Environment lives at the unit, one tap from Home. Inspection no longer carries sensors, batch tracker or maintenance.
- A sensor with no numeric reading is omitted, never shown as 0. A unit with neither readings nor devices has no entrance. A controllable device is independent of readings.
- Readings: Temperature °C, Humidity %, Ammonia ppm NH₃, each with last-reading time, a Today or 7-day trend, low and high, and a reading-history table.
- Fan: Auto (follows the unit schedule) or Manual with a speed 0-100 in steps of 5; an explicit Apply; everything disabled offline with "Reconnect to change device settings."
- Maintenance is unit-scoped: open-issue count; Report issue (equipment, location in the unit, note, all required); issue detail with Mark resolved. The open count feeds the Maintenance chip on the unit hub.
- All data is sample; no command is sent to equipment (PREVIEW badges).

## Scope

In: sensors, fan, maintenance list, report and resolve.

Out: real sensor feeds, alerts and thresholds, photos or assignees on issues, devices other than the fan, cross-unit views.

## Decisions

- Decided (ASTRA-HOME-DIRECTION): environment and maintenance belong to unit Home; Inspection does not repeat them.
- Open: alert thresholds and who is told; whether the Maintenance chip should link to the list (today it is reached only through Toolbox); whether issues get priority, photo, assignee and a resolver stamp; which other devices are controllable; whether Farrowing and Breeding units get an entrance (the sample has none).

elements.name: Task card · state
elements.shows: Farrowing: "2 sows farrowing · 4 due today"; Piglet processing: "Next care · Tomorrow"

states.when: Farrowing, no live sow, late > 0. No sample reaches it: Home never supplies late
states.shows: "N sows past expected date" · "No final record"

states.when: Not farrowing and the due count in the scope is > 0
states.shows: "N <task label>" (sows ready to check, sows ready for service, litters with care due); one supporting line: pregnancy "N scheduled later" (unrecorded minus due), heat and return-heat "Current round", else none. Farrowing with no live sow: "N sows due today", no supporting line

states.when: Due > 0 and f.overdue > 0. No sample reaches it: Home never supplies overdue
states.shows: Supporting line "N past due" replaces the other line; rank 1

states.when: f.rechecks > 0, or f.first and f.repeat supplied. No sample reaches it
states.shows: "N rechecks due" (before "scheduled later"); breeding "N first · N repeat"

states.when: ?work=ready and the card has a completion bar (heat and return-heat are excluded)
states.shows: Quiet "All required work recorded", bar full, "Review & complete task" row; timing pill and footer hidden

states.when: Ready and closureBlockedBy is set. No sample reaches it
states.shows: "Waiting for <task> to close", quiet style

states.when: f.unitComplete is set. No sample reaches it
states.shows: "Unit work complete · task still open"

states.when: The card's preview state is waiting (Pregnancy Batch 32, Breeding, Piglet processing), ?work=waiting, or nothing is due or live in the scope (Farrowing in Unit 8)
states.shows: "<Next> · <time>": "Next care", "Next checks", "Next service", "Next expected", "Next check" + "Tomorrow" (nextAt of a day or more) or hh:mm; no count, sorted under "Next"

states.when: Nothing due and no nextLabel. No sample reaches it: every sample card has a nextAt
states.shows: "Waiting for heat confirmations" (breeding), "Waiting for next scheduled care" (piglet), "Waiting for farrowing records" (postpartum), else "No work due now"

states.when: Heat or return-heat card whose preview state is round-complete (Return-heat Batch 30, Heat Batch 35) or ?work=round-complete
states.shows: "Round complete · Next check · 14:30", no progress bar. Other tasks fall back to Waiting
Compact receipt at the bottom (see Closed task card)

elements.logic: Evaluated in this order: closed, alert, task-specific work due, ready, unit complete, next scheduled action. A full bar, a finished unit or one full session never proves the whole task is ready. Home's sample data forces Piglet processing to "Waiting" (cardFields.piglet27.state) so its due counts of 2 + 2 are ignored unless ?work=active.
elements.rule: Counts are unique animals or litters in the selected scope, never procedures. The headline is what is actionable now; it is not total minus completed when eligibility depends on time.

elements.name: Task card · headline and supporting line
elements.shows: 2 sows farrowing · 4 due today
elements.logic: Value = sum of the sample "due" counts over the scope (Farrowing due {6:2, 7:2, 8:0}); "live" = the next unrecorded sow in each unit except Unit 8, so Overview 2, Unit 6 1, Unit 7 1, Unit 8 none. Only one supporting line is shown, by task: pregnancy and postpartum "N rechecks due" else "N scheduled later" (unrecorded minus due); breeding "N first · N repeat"; heat and return-heat "Current round". Label takes the singular for 1 ("1 sow farrowing"). With no live sow, due today becomes the headline with no supporting line; with nothing due the card is Waiting.

elements.name: Task card · progress bar
elements.shows: Farrowings recorded · 7 / 18 sows
elements.logic: Named aggregate progress: items with a recorded result over all items in the scope (Farrowing Overview 7/18, Unit 6 4/8, Unit 7 1/6, Unit 8 2/4; Piglet processing counts pens, 1/8). Bar width = value/total. Home forces a plain completion bar even where the task itself shows a distribution. Heat and return-heat have no completion bar, and "recorded in heat" is an outcome, not progress. The bar is hidden on upcoming cards.

elements.name: Task card · timing pill and footer
elements.shows: Day 2 of 7 · Across 3 units · View task
elements.logic: The pill is the position in the batch window (cardFields day, days), "Today" when the window is one day; it is context, not a completion measure, and not the litters' own age. It is hidden on a Ready card. "Across N units" = units that carry the task (not units with work due); in a unit scope the footer is replaced by an arrow in the header and the card opens that unit's task.

elements.name: "Next" sub-heading and card order
elements.shows: Next
elements.logic: Cards sort by attention rank: live farrowing or alert 0, overdue 1, due 2, ready to complete 2.5, waiting 3 (earliest next event first), closed 4. Equal ranks keep their order so the list does not jump. "Next" is printed once above the first quiet card (waiting, round complete or upcoming).

features.prd:
# Workbench 工作台

## Problem

A worker opens the app to know what to do now, not how the farm is doing. Home must answer "what is ready, where" at a glance, let the worker work either by task across units or by place inside one unit, and show what is saved on the phone when there is no signal. The old Figma (首页 › 工作台) says the same: a workbench, not a data page.

## Who

Daily floor workers in a section (Breeding, Gestation, Farrowing, Nursery): gloved, one-handed, often offline. A supervisor completes or ends tasks from the same cards.

## Anchor

None. Home has no lifecycle of its own; each card inherits the lifecycle of its task. Screens are grouped by scope: section Overview, unit, drawers, task preview, settings.

## Rules

- The screen is "Today's work": one card per task instance in the chosen section, ordered by attention rank (live exception, overdue, due, ready to complete, waiting by earliest next event, closed last). Equal ranks keep their order so cards do not jump.
- Evaluation order per card (HOME-TASK-DISPLAY-RULES): closed receipt; confirmed exception; task-specific work due; all required work recorded (only a permitted whole-task closure gets "Review & complete task"); unit work finished while others remain; next scheduled action.
- A card has identity (task, batch, context), timing ("Day N of N", contextual, never a completion measure), one headline count (what is actionable now), at most one supporting line, a named aggregate progress bar, and in the Overview a footer "Across N units · View task". The main count is never total minus done.
- Counts are unique animals or litters in the selected scope. A unit narrows the counts, never the batch time.
- Task-specific rules: Farrowing = underway, past expected date, due today, next expected; Piglet processing = litters with care due, next care, waiting; Pregnancy = open windows, then next check; Heat and Return-heat show no completion bar for observation.
- Unit scope: inspection, attention, environment and devices entrances sit at the unit; Inspection owns the pen walk.
- Offline: records saved on the device are shown with a count and the connection state; upload is explicit.
- Closed tasks never revive due counts.

## Scope

In: section chooser, Overview, unit picker, unit hub, card states (due, waiting, round complete, ready, closed), Saved work drawer, task preview, end-early confirmation, closed-task receipt.

Out: Assistant, Scan and Toolbox (other pages of the same prototype); task detail pages (their own features); Environment & devices (its own feature). Language and Log out exist in the old design and are not built here (placeholder).

## Decisions

- Decided: one Overview plus unit scope; Assistant has no badge on Home; the last section is remembered; the unit picker has no search (about 15 units at most); completion stays inside the task.
- Open: where language and log out live; what the real "Not designed yet" page shows per task; whether ready-to-complete shows a review before closing; how the real queue feeds Saved work; what "Day N of N" means for tasks with no batch window.
- Open (data): the Home sample batches (Piglet processing Batch 27, 8 pens, 2 units) do not match the piglet-processing prototype it opens (Batch 40, 12 pens).

features.prd:
# Farrowing (分娩)

Section: Tasks · Platform: mobile · Prototype: `ux/system/farrowing-astra-concept.html?layout=focus` · Rulings: `ux/research/farrowing/RULINGS.md` (headings quoted below) · State contract: `ux/system/farrowing-contract.html`

## Problem

A sow can farrow for hours, across shifts, with wet gloves, one hand on the crate and no signal guarantee. The worker needs to count the piglets as they arrive without ever feeling the count is unsaved, record the dead by cause, fix a wrong figure without erasing the first one, and close the litter with a few deliberate facts. The supervisor needs the same records to roll up into one task: how many sows have farrowed, which are still going, which are still waiting, and a clean way to end the batch's farrowing task. The old UI scattered these over several screens and corrections had many doors; this feature keeps one familiar flow with a clearer place for every number.

## Who

- Farrowing-house worker (gloved, one-handed, often at night): counts, records deaths, finishes litters.
- Next-shift worker: reads the room list to see who is farrowing and who was last touched, then continues from the same record.
- Unit lead / supervisor: reads the unit and task progress, corrects posted figures, ends the task.
- Anyone may amend a finished record; provenance (stamp, original kept) replaces permissions.

## Anchor

The anchor is the **sow** (her litter session). Statuses: **Awaiting** (nothing recorded; live total zero) → **Farrowing** (live total above zero, not finished) → **Finished** (Born locked). Exit: **Died** (the sow's death ends the session without Finish; she stays in the room as a Done-register row). Reachable in any status: the **Room list** and the **Farrowing log**. Task bands: **Task in progress** (the whole-task overview) and **Ending the task** (the four End task reviews and the receipt).

Status is derived, never set by a ceremony: "registers derive from the live total (posted + open pending)" (RULINGS *Starting and ending a session*).

## Rules

From RULINGS.md, quoted short:

- **Model**: "Born = Alive + Σ Dead + fostered out − fostered in. Derived, never entered, locks at Finish."
- **Model**: Alive is one classless number; "+ is free; − drains pending and clamps at the floor" (B\* minus the dead recorded). Born can never drop silently.
- **Model**: five default dead types plus Other (stillborn, mummified, crushed, scours, starve-out).
- **Model**: "No WHEN anywhere, absolutely … The stamp is the date."
- **Model**: "Classification (weak/deformed) happens at Finish, commits per tap"; "Healthy has no form row"; litter weight and assisted are optional.
- **Model**: Active row line 2 is "born 14 · 1h ago · G.H"; "No staleness tracking on Active sows"; the interval chip is retired. "Every litter row carries its three numbers" (alive · dead, born).
- **Model**: "The overdue signal ends at the first record"; rows speak in days from due (due = service + 114), never gestation day; "Overdue · 3 days" colours only the number.
- **Model**: "The hero owns the total; the receipt owns the change" (`Saved · +4 this visit`).
- **Surfaces & entrances**: "ONE dead drawer product-wide", opened by Record dead; staged: Save commits, Back keeps the draft, Clear discards.
- **Surfaces & entrances**: "ONE correction door: Edit … ONE SCREEN"; "What Edit adjusts: the observations, never the derivation"; a missed fact is a recording, never an Edit.
- **Surfaces & entrances**: "Type-to-set is retired on count figures"; one stepper shape, − n +, everywhere.
- **Surfaces & entrances**: "Identity is sheet-first … the room row offers no sow-page target."
- **Surfaces & entrances**: "`Finish` is `Finish farrowing`"; the hold-to-lock is "the second guard".
- **Starting and ending a session**: "Farrowing starts at the first recorded event — full stop."
- **Starting and ending a session**: the sow's death lives in the drawer (`Piglets · The sow`), "hold-to-commit"; "She stays in the room".
- **Starting and ending a session**: "A non-empty ledger is never unreachable"; a draft never crosses the lock.
- **After the lock**: "The record face IS the record"; "One ledger surface, the Farrowing record page"; "History is the chevron on the fact line"; "The correction mark is the amber value".
- **After the lock**: Born is amended through the Edit ceremony popup (`More born` / `Count was wrong`); "Anyone may amend born post-lock — open ✎, stamped, no role gate." Fostering is **parked**.
- **Names and glyphs**: "words carry actions, icons carry objects"; dates speak relative within the week.
- **Piglet processing, Round 5**: all tasks look the same (farrowing's skeleton); "The exit word is always **Back**."
- **Owner calls for this atlas**: *Edit record* is editing while she is still farrowing; *Correct born* exists only after farrowing has finished. Home's Farrowing card and Choose unit both land on the room list.

## Scope

In:

- Room list: unit card, whole-task card, Awaiting / Active / Done / All tabs, due and parity filter, pen grouping, Go to pen, Scan ear tag, Search.
- The sow sheet in its faces: Before first count, Counting, Finish (and its blocked form), Locked record, Sow died.
- Death entry (piglets and the sow), Edit record, Edit of a finished litter and the Correct born popup, the Farrowing log.
- Whole-task overview, End task reviews (blocked, awaiting, all finished, outcomes) and the task receipt.
- Farrowing's rows on the pig's Actions sheet (Edit litter record, Record miscarriage, Mark not in pig).

Out:

- Fostering (parked until the owner reopens it).
- Piglet processing and its identity work (separate feature; Move opens after the lock).
- The sow page itself and the rest of the Actions sheet (pig-profile).
- Pen tools reachable from a pen header (feed guidance, equipment fault, pen note, pen log): present in the prototype, unclear whose feature; recorded in the Room list issues.
- Console reporting, anomaly queues, per-hand audit views, merge-review UI, notifications.
- Role gates, batch-close disposition doors beyond what the End task reviews show.

## Decisions

- Born is derived and frozen at Finish; Alive and the dead types are the observations — RULINGS *Model*.
- Born floor: "+" free, "−" clamps at B\* minus current dead — RULINGS *Model*.
- Five dead types plus Other; no WHEN chips — RULINGS *Model*.
- Weak and deformed asked at Finish only; Healthy derived — RULINGS *Model*.
- Row line 2 carries recency in words; interval chip retired — RULINGS *Model*.
- Overdue signal stops at the first record — RULINGS *Model*.
- Days from due on rows, gestation day on the sheet header only — RULINGS *Model*.
- Receipt `Saved · +4 this visit`; hero numeral plain, no typing — RULINGS *Model*.
- Edit folds weak, deformed, weight and assisted into one `At finish` row — RULINGS *Model*.
- Dead drawer is the only dead entrance, staged (Back/Clear/Save) — RULINGS *Surfaces & entrances*.
- Edit is the only correction door and one screen — RULINGS *Surfaces & entrances*.
- Count figures are stepper-only — RULINGS *Surfaces & entrances*.
- Sheet-first identity: only the sheet header opens the sow page — RULINGS *Surfaces & entrances*.
- Exit grammar: bars hold exits only; Finish farrowing is a hold — RULINGS *Surfaces & entrances*.
- Farrowing starts at the first record; no started mark — RULINGS *Starting and ending a session*.
- The sow's death is a hold-to-commit mode of the drawer; she stays in the room — RULINGS *Starting and ending a session*.
- Merge contract: signed deltas, flag instead of silently applying a breach — RULINGS *Starting and ending a session*.
- Fostering parked — RULINGS *After the lock*.
- The locked record is designed as a record, with one ledger page — RULINGS *After the lock*.
- Anyone may amend Born after the lock — RULINGS *After the lock*.
- Words for actions, icons for objects — RULINGS *Names and glyphs*.
- Relative dates inside a week — RULINGS *Names and glyphs*.
- Farrowing's skeleton is the model for all tasks; exit word Back — RULINGS *Piglet processing, Round 5*.
- Task end: manual, hold-to-commit with receipt, blocked while farrowing is open — RULINGS *Piglet processing, Q5*; closure details in `ux/research/farrowing/ASTRA-TASK-CLOSURE.md`.
- Edit record vs Correct born split by status; Home entries land on the room list — owner calls for this atlas.

features.prd:
# Piglet processing 仔猪处理

## Problem

After farrowing, each litter owes a schedule by age-day (iron, dock tail, castrate, coccidiosis, and the identification step the farm requires). The worker records it pen by pen, with paper habits and dirty gloves. The task must show what each pen still needs today, record a pen with one tick per item and one Submit, and keep the litter's count honest through deaths, moves and counts, all looking exactly like Farrowing.

## Who

Piglet-care workers walking the pens (farmers, not tech-savvy; Round 8). A supervisor ends the task.

## Anchor

Pen (a sow with her litter). Its status is derived, not stored: Coming (every step still ahead), To do (anything due or partly given), Late (a step past its window; shown over To do), Done (nothing left, nothing ahead). A dead sow adds a red chip but the litter stays on its schedule. The task has its own band: in progress, then ended (End task by hold).

## Rules

- Windows in pen age days: Iron 2-4, Dock tail 2-4, Castrate 3-7, Coccidiosis 3-5, ID 3-7. Outside the window a record is stamped early or late automatically; early counts on time (Round 1 Q6).
- One tick per item, one Submit. Fewer piglets than alive asks one reason (weak or sick); the rest stay on the list.
- Identity follows the farm: tag every piglet, notch every piglet, breeders only, or no ID (then no ID step at all). ID is always available on a pen and is also a step on the ID day. One piglet at a time, tag or notch; sex required here; weight optional (Rounds 1, 7, 10).
- Alive = born, minus dead, minus moved out, plus moved in. Set count only adjusts the record; the difference goes to the batch-level "N piglets unaccounted", not to the pen (Round 9). Move offers only the pens of the batch and asks what the piglets already had.
- Same look as Farrowing: list row = id + one chip + one headline + one meta line; the pen opens as a sheet; Back, not Close (Round 5). End task is a hold and reviews in numbers (Round 1 Q5).
- Two phones recording the same item: first record wins, the second is kept as a note (simplification, not yet confirmed).
- In the rulings but not in this prototype: End blocked while the batch's farrowing is open; corrections after End; the shared dead picker; Edit; bulk recording with a Finish hold.

## Scope

In: pen list with job chips, pen sheet, Piglets list, Give IDs, boars and gilts, litter weight, death, move, set count, pen log, End task.

Out: recording several pens at once (Round 9 keeps bulk as chips, but the prototype has only the filter), farrowing's Born figure, the weaning handoff, breeder ranking (placeholder only), multi-sow pens, fostering outside the batch.

## Decisions

Decided:
- Same look as Farrowing, pruned to its density; farmers first; restrict rather than add mechanisms (Rounds 5, 8).
- Set count just adjusts; no nurse sows outside the task; Move only within the batch (Round 9).
- Tagging per farm scheme; per-piglet work and breeder selection may become universal; ranking is a placeholder (Rounds 7, 10).
- Verbs Record, Edit, Set count, End task (Q11, provisional).

Open (HANDOFF, needs the owner):
1. The seven simplifications: moves within the batch with Yes/No; count = reason or "count was wrong"; first-in-wins sync; cut nurse sow outside the task; cut after-End evidence; cut fine-grained corrections; keep bulk. The prototype implements 1, 2, 3 and 5 and keeps bulk only as a filter.
2. Rules the builder interpreted: ID window day 3-7; the Tag chip filters only (no bulk tagging); Move asks "Have tags?"; "Done picking" may close with no breeders; a pen with nothing due yet counts as done; losses come off untreated piglets first; a higher count just corrects; sheet records past the window are marked late automatically; bulk pre-ticks only pens fully inside the window.
3. Candidate approvals at close: task skeleton parts (ADR 0003, with Chips) and candidates 2 (ADR 0002) with four nods (keyboard two-step hold, one 35% sweep, Row code 600, 64 px optional radio row).
4. Build path: carry the simplified flows into the full task, or promote simple/ to be the task.
5. Where per-piglet work (ID, weigh, sex, breeder) lives as a universal feature (Round 10 direction only; proposal first).
6. How a farm's ID scheme is configured (Round 1 Q3); in the prototype it is a Demo switch outside the phone.

features.prd:
# Feed plan 饲喂计划

## Problem

Feed is guidance for the worker, not a task to tick off. The worker needs to see what a pen and each pig is fed today and to change it for one pig, several pigs or several pens in one move. The old Figma has no feed plan screen; this feature is new and is built inside the Inspection prototype.

## Who

The worker on the walk, who reads today's feed on the pen header, and the worker who must adjust it after a finding (a thin sow, a sick pen). Sows in a trough pen and in a station pen are covered; ad-lib pens are read-only.

## Anchor

No anchor. A pig's feed is always in one of four states (follow the curve, adjusted by a percentage, held at a fixed amount, stopped), but the states do not drive other work, so the screens are grouped as Read, Several pens, Adjust and On the walk list.

## Rules

- Feed is guidance: formula, amount, timing. It creates no completion event; the Record as done and refill actions were removed (ROUND-3).
- A pig's allowance = base amount from the curve x factor, or a held amount, or 0 when stopped. A pen's total is the sum of its pigs.
- The editor changes feed by a percentage of the curve from -50% to +50%, or holds the amount, or stops feed. The percentage replaces existing adjustments.
- Ad-lib pigs, dead sows and pigs with no plan are listed as blocked with the reason and are never changed.
- An end date, if given, is today or later. A note is optional.
- Opening the editor from a pen or from ticked pens captures the pigs of those pens; the same editor serves pens, ticked pigs and one pig.
- Keep the feeding program (the animal's plan) separate from the feed formula (the product) - ASTRA-FEED-PLAN-FIELDS.

## Scope

In: Pen feeding (reading), ad-lib pen, the several-pens entry, the Adjust feed editor and its end date and note, the pig's feed plan with the base curve, and how a pen-wide increase, decrease or hold reads on the walk list.

Out: the pen header on the walk (inspection), the Feeding block on the pig record (pig-profile), body-condition findings that used to link to feed (health-record). Feed inventory, purchase, supplier and formula authoring belong to management screens.

## Decisions

- One editor for every scope; only the target changes.
- Percentage limits of -50% and +50%, slider steps of 5%.
- The base curve is a sample (day 35 to 56 around the pig's base amount) and makes no claim about real feed.

Open (recorded on the screens as issues):

- Brand, supplier, energy (ME or NE), protein and lysine proposed in ASTRA-FEED-PLAN-FIELDS are not drawn; units for protein and lysine are unconfirmed.
- Saving a change silently ends the link between a body-condition finding and its feed adjustment.
- Three ways to return to the curve (mode, 0%, Reset).
- "Formula due" on the pen header has no screen that explains it.
- A held amount shows only a tag; the kg is in a tooltip.

features.prd:
# Inspection 巡检

## Problem

A worker walks one unit and has to see every pig, spot the ones that need care or feed attention, and record what they find without leaving the place they are standing. Today's old UI spreads this over many screens in the Inspection Figma file. The built prototype (`ux/system/inspection-astra-concept.html`) puts it in one list with a dock, but several parts of it are built and never reachable (unit summary, sensors, batch tracker, equipment faults), and the list repeats facts that the pig record also shows.

## Who

The barn worker doing the morning or evening walk, often wearing gloves, one hand free. The supervisor reads the same list to see what was recorded ("Log", "Check in"). The unit is the scope: there is no cohort.

## Anchor

No anchor. The walk has no lifecycle that changes what work is available: it can be checked in again at any time ("Check in again"), and nothing is blocked before or after. The screens are therefore grouped by what the worker is doing: walk the list, open a pen, select and act, unit batches, unit environment and equipment (built, not reachable), finish.

## Rules

- Selection is not an inspection result. A pig checkbox never selects its pen; a pen checkbox selects the pen and the pigs shown (ROUND-3).
- Notes belong to the pen, not to its pigs. A pen has one note; closing it moves it into the pen log.
- Feed is guidance, not a completion checklist: nothing on the walk can be "done" for feed.
- The stage on a row is days in the stage, never lifetime age; the walk date is fixed in the sample (12 Sep 2026).
- Care is the only editable condition state; attention is derived from it (ASTRA-BULK-ACTIONS).
- One Actions sheet for one pig or many; Production actions exist only for one pig.
- Finishing a walk records that the unit was walked; it does not mark pigs healthy or tasks done.

## Scope

In: the unit walk list (lens All / Health / Feed, filter, pen map, find and scan), the pen sheet with note and log, the selection and Actions sheet, the walk log and check-in, the unit batches that change the stage text, and the built-but-unreachable unit summary, sensors, batch sheet and equipment fault flow.

Out (owned by other features): the pig record and its actions (pig-profile), feed reading and editing (feed-plan), conditions, care and treatment (health-record). The Farrowing task is opened from here but belongs to Tasks.

## Decisions

Taken from the research notes and the code:

- The roster shows every pig (the earlier "quiet pigs collapsed" idea was dropped) with an identity line and one line of tags.
- Home opens this page through the "Inspect unit" card with the unit kept in the link; Back returns to Home with the unit.
- Pen map copies Farrowing's four-column, six-row map and 350 ms hold-to-peek.

Open (recorded on the screens as issues):

- The unit summary card (pig and pen counts, faults, sensors, batch tracker) is in the code and not placed on the walk. Draw it or remove it.
- Equipment faults have a full report-and-resolve flow but no control reaches it.
- "Health" and "Feed" lens counts do not say what they count.
- The care level shows only by icon and colour on a row.
- Fixed author "G. Hansen" and times 06:40 and 09:41 stand in for the signed-in worker and real times.

features.prd:
# Pig profile 猪只详情

## Problem

When a worker taps a pig they need, in this order: what needs attention, what to do next, who she is, how she is fed, where to read more, and the actions they can take. The old Figma draws pig detail twice: inside Inspection and in the pig list (猪只列表) file. The built version (inside the Inspection prototype) is one sheet with six blocks and many repeated facts.

## Who

A worker on the walk or in a task who reaches a single pig; the same sheet opens inside Farrowing's sow drawer. A supervisor reading history uses Production stats, Origin and Log.

## Anchor

No anchor. The record is the same for a pig at any stage; what changes is which blocks and which actions apply. Screens are grouped as The record, Read more, Actions - Production, Actions - General and Actions - Unavailable.

## Rules

- Human-entered records lead; derived plans and stable facts sit in reading sections.
- The blocks follow the animal type (Sow cycle, Gilt breeding, Boar breeding, Piglet growth, Growth).
- An empty production-average section is absent; facts missing from the registry show a dash.
- The Actions sheet has three groups, Production, Health and General. Production is for one pig only and holds only the rows that fit her stage and tasks; blocked rows are listed with the reason in "Unavailable actions".
- Farrowing opens the shared health and measurement flows rather than copying them; it adds its own Production rows when embedded (piglet processing, piglet deaths, count reconciliation, fostering, litter edit, remove from batch, not in pig, transfer).
- Not in pig, miscarriage and batch removal take a sow out of her batch and return her to rebreed watch; saved records are kept.
- Weight, temperature and backfat take one value per pig.
- A dead sow offers a note only.

## Scope

In: the record (full, partial, empty, with tasks), Production stats and a batch record, Origin, the pig Log, the Actions sheet for one pig, the task outcome form, miscarriage, batch membership, the measurement menu and forms, body condition, notes and the unavailable list.

Entry points: Inspection (a pig row, search or scan), Tasks (a sow in the Farrowing room list), Pigs (the pig list; that feature is a placeholder written elsewhere, so this entry has no source screen yet).

Out: health forms and findings (health-record), feed editing and the pig's feed plan (feed-plan), the unit walk (inspection). Transfer sow, Mark not in pig and Remove from batch render only inside Farrowing's drawer; they are named on the Actions screen but not drawn as screens here.

## Decisions

- One Actions sheet for one pig or twenty; the Production group appears only for one.
- Tasks are shown as cards on the record and as rows in Actions; Farrowing and Piglet processing open the Farrowing task.
- Body condition is recorded from Measurements & condition and creates a health finding with Monitor care.

Open (recorded on the screens as issues):

- Next task and Batch are repeated in the task card, the grid and the type block; stage and days appear in the header, the grid and the type block.
- Age is in days for a sow.
- Saving a reading or a note returns to the walk list, not to the pig record; the task, miscarriage and batch forms return to the record.
- The pig's lifetime figures (litters, born total, rates) are in the data but not shown.
- Mark-not-in-pig, remove-from-batch and transfer cannot be reviewed outside Farrowing.

features.prd:
# Health record 健康管理

## Problem

The worker records a disease or symptom on one or many pigs, says what to do about it (care), records treatment, and later closes the record as recovered or entered in error. The old Figma draws health three times: in Inspection (add and remove disease or symptom), in the pig list (health management) and in the 健康与治疗 treatment file. The Inspection prototype is the one built version.

## Who

The worker on the walk who finds a sick pig, and the worker who gives treatment or vaccination as a task. A supervisor reads the care levels on the list.

## Anchor

Anchor: the Finding (one condition on one pig).

- Needs attention: care is Monitor, Treat in place or Move to hospital pen. Shown as a row on top of the pig record, with the care level and the day.
- Ongoing, no action needed: recorded and visible as a tag until it is resolved.
- Closed: Recovered, or Entered in error. The case leaves the active list and stays in the pig's log.

Recording, editing, treatment and the pickers can happen in any status.

## Rules

- Diseases and symptoms are one searchable catalogue (9 disease categories; symptoms by body area and body system), for one pig or many. A name that is not in the catalogue can be added as a custom item under a chosen category.
- Care is the only editable condition state: No action needed, Monitor, Treat in place, Move to hospital pen. Attention is derived: every choice except No action needed needs attention.
- Existing findings keep their original start date; adding a condition a pig already has changes nothing.
- Bulk edits preview each pig's change, let a pig be excluded, leave pigs without the condition unchanged, and save only changed rows.
- Treatment records medicine actually given: medicine, method, unit and a dose above 0, a shared dose with a per-pig override, and optional brand, linked condition and note. One record per included pig.
- A treatment started from a Health task (vaccination) lists vaccines only and completes the task on Save.
- A blocked action is listed with the reason, never dropped.
- Recovery keeps the case in history; entered in error marks a correction. Recovering a finding linked to a feed adjustment ends that adjustment.
- Hospital pen is a care choice only; no move is made.

## Scope

In: the pig record as a health view (needs attention, ongoing, several ongoing, care levels), the finding and its edit and resolve forms, Record health with its catalogue picker, Care instructions and Edit conditions, Resolve conditions, Record treatment with the medicine picker (and the brand and condition choosers inside it).

Out: sow death and mortality reports (separate features), the pig record itself (pig-profile), feed changes (feed-plan). Health tags on the walk row belong to inspection.

## Decisions

- Care replaced the older triage and status fields; one select drives both.
- Medicines, brands and units are a sample catalogue until farm configuration exists.
- Treatment never implies identical doses across pigs.

Open (recorded on the screens as issues):

- The default Care is No action needed, so the shortest path records a fever as a non-alert.
- Two rows (Edit conditions and Care instructions) open the same form; Edit finding and Resolve or remove touch the same record for one pig; naming differs between Resolve conditions and Resolve or remove.
- Duration is "Day 2" for attention and "120 days" for ongoing; the day count never advances in the prototype.
- "Recorded — · —" shows empty dashes for unknown date and author.
- The catalogue starts on Symptoms and needs three taps to reach an item; there is no recent or common list.

Research rule: segmented = a fixed set of 2-5 views of the same data; filter chips = narrowing a list by tags from a dynamic set. Here the set is dynamic (only the jobs due today, 2-7 chips), goes past Segment's cap of 4, scrolls, and each chip is a tag (a job), not a state. It already exists as TaskChips; make it generic (any list narrowed by tag), raise the chip to 48px, and keep the rule "never chips and a lens on one list". Open question for the owner: "Done" is a state, not a tag; it sits in the chip row only because the list cannot also carry a lens.

backlog.title: All 7 environment screens open the unit hub, not their own screen
backlog.detail: None of the environment screens has steps or a preset, so each opens the Home unit page instead of the sensors, fan, maintenance or issue views. The atlas shows the wrong picture for the whole feature.

backlog.title: Does Inspection keep its built equipment-fault and unit-environment screens?
backlog.detail: Environment's PRD says Inspection no longer carries sensors or maintenance, but Inspection still holds built unit-detail, pen-faults, fault-report, fault-resolve and sensor screens, and its section text says equipment and environment sit there. Two homes for the same faults.
options: Remove the Inspection fault and sensor screens; Environment owns them
Keep a per-pen fault entry in Inspection that writes the same record
Keep both and merge later
backlog.recommendation: Remove from Inspection; keep one fault record owned by Environment, and let the pen sheet link to it.

backlog.title: Who is told when a reading is out of range?
backlog.detail: Alert thresholds, recipients and the source of real readings are not defined anywhere; the page shows only sample history.
options: Out of scope for the prototype; mark as backend follow-up
Fixed farm-wide thresholds, flag on the unit hub
Per-unit thresholds set by a supervisor
backlog.recommendation: Mark out of scope now; decide thresholds before real data is wired.

backlog.title: Can the fan be set offline, and is 0% allowed?
backlog.detail: Auto/Manual and Apply are disabled offline, so a worker in a room without signal cannot change the fan. Speed 0 needs no confirmation or limit. Neither rule is decided.
options: Disabled offline, 0% blocked below a minimum
Queue the command and show it as pending
Allow 0% with a confirmation
backlog.recommendation: Keep disabled offline (a queued command to equipment is unsafe); set a minimum speed or confirm 0%.

backlog.title: Offline note repeats three times; last reading fixed at 09:40
backlog.detail: The offline message shows under the chart, on the Devices tag and under the fan; every sensor shows one 09:40 time while the status bar says 9:41. Say it once, with a time per sensor.

backlog.title: Do Farrowing and Breeding units get an environment entrance?
backlog.detail: The sample gives them no sensors, so the card is absent, but old-design farrowing rooms carry sensors. A farrowing worker then has no environment or maintenance door at all.
options: Same entrance in every unit; empty state when no devices
Only where the unit has sensors or devices (today)
Always show Maintenance, show Environment only with data
backlog.recommendation: Always show Maintenance (equipment fails anywhere); show Environment only with data.

backlog.title: Should the Maintenance chip open the issue list?
backlog.detail: The Maintenance chip on the unit hub opens Inspection; the list is only reachable through Toolbox, which exists only inside a unit. Two taps and an unexpected destination.
options: Chip opens Maintenance
Chip stays a signal, Toolbox is the door
Remove the chip, put the count on the Environment card
backlog.recommendation: Chip opens the Maintenance list; keep Toolbox as a second door.

backlog.title: Equipment and location are free text with no picklist
backlog.detail: The reporter types equipment and location, though the unit's pens and devices are known. Typing with gloves is slow and produces unmatchable names. Use pen and equipment pickers with Other.

backlog.title: What does an issue record beyond open and resolved?
backlog.detail: No photo, priority, assignee, resolver, resolve time or note; a resolved issue cannot be reopened and stays listed forever.
options: Keep minimal: add resolver and time only
Add photo and a resolve note
Add priority and assignee for supervisors
backlog.recommendation: Add resolver, time and optional note and allow Reopen; defer photo, priority and assignee.

backlog.title: 'Only resolved' issues state has no designed empty view
backlog.detail: When every issue is resolved the list shows dimmed cards with '0 open issues' instead of the empty state; the rule for when old resolved issues leave the list is missing.

backlog.title: Where do Language and Log out live?
backlog.detail: The old Figma has Select language, Log out and a result screen; the prototype has no control and no entry, and the screen has no URL so it cannot be shown.
options: Header profile button
Toolbox settings row
Bottom of the section chooser
backlog.recommendation: Toolbox settings row: the header is already full with the Assistant.

backlog.title: How does the saved-work drawer relate to the Data sync feature?
backlog.detail: The old Figma has a data-sync list, per-pig and per-treatment detail with conflict states, and upload screens; the drawer only shows a flat queue and upload. Which one owns conflicts and detail?
options: Drawer is the entry; Data sync screens become its row detail
Separate Data sync page behind the drawer
Drop conflict handling for now
backlog.recommendation: Drawer is the entry, rows open Data sync detail; design data-sync once.

backlog.title: Nothing records into the saved-work queue
backlog.detail: The three records are fictional; records made in Farrowing, Piglet processing or Inspection never appear. A developer cannot tell what is queued, in what order, or how a conflict is reported.

backlog.title: Saved-work card tops the page and pushes today's work down
backlog.detail: While offline, a full-width card sits above the first task card on every Home view. A farmer's first question is 'what is due', not 'what is unsent'. The count could live in the header.

backlog.title: Unit hub stacks too many items before the task cards
backlog.detail: The unit view shows saved work, Inspect unit with three attention chips and an environment strip, then tasks. Information repeats (the same Health 3 and Feed 3 in every unit) and the Maintenance chip signals a different feature. Rank what the worker must see first.

backlog.title: Unit hub 'Checked Yesterday' drops who and when
backlog.detail: The strip keeps only the first segment of the check stamp; the direction doc asks for last-check time.

backlog.title: 'Across N units' and the timing pill repeat on every card
backlog.detail: The footer count means units that carry the task, not units with work, and repeats on every card. On a long list the footer adds a line and little information.

backlog.title: Seven card states are never reached by any sample
backlog.detail: Alert, Past expected, Overdue, Rechecks or first/repeat, Waiting for another task, Unit work complete and Waiting-next-unknown are coded but no data reaches them, so their design is untested.

backlog.title: Piglet card disagrees with the prototype it opens
backlog.detail: Home says Batch 27, 8 pens, next care tomorrow; opening it lands on Batch 40, 12 pens, 6 due. The card also mixes litters ('4 litters with care due') and pens ('1 / 8 pens').

backlog.title: Gestation card shows 'Today' and 'Tomorrow' for the same batch
backlog.detail: Batch 32 pill says Today while the body says Next checks, Tomorrow. The date is also fixed sample text, 'Thu, 8 Jul'.

backlog.title: Heat check shows the same 20 twice
backlog.detail: The card reads '20 sows to check' and '0 / 20 sows in heat': a count and an outcome that looks like progress.

backlog.title: 'Task types ready' counts waiting tasks as ready
backlog.detail: The chooser says '2 task types ready' when tasks may only be waiting; the unit sheet's '2 tasks' counts unrecorded rows, not due work. Farrowing also reads 19 pigs here but 18 sows on its Overview.

backlog.title: Current unit row has no tint or check
backlog.detail: The direction doc asks for a tint and check; the code only sets aria-current, so a worker cannot see which unit is chosen.

backlog.title: 'Due now' only exists as an accessible label
backlog.detail: When work is due the pill still reads 'Day 3 of 7'; the due state is invisible beyond the count.

backlog.title: Tasks without a page open an empty stand-in
backlog.detail: Every task other than Farrowing and Piglet processing lands on 'This task page is still to come', with no work shown. The wording differs from the research name 'Not designed yet'. Eight Tasks features are placeholders behind it.

backlog.title: Does completing a task show a review first?
backlog.detail: Complete task closes at once. The rules ask for a review before closing.
options: No review, plain confirm
Review sheet with what is recorded and what is open, then hold to complete
Review only when something is unrecorded
backlog.recommendation: Review sheet then hold to complete, like Farrowing's end task.

backlog.title: End task early states no consequence
backlog.detail: The drawer says only that unfinished work remains incomplete; the rules say each task must show its batch and backfill effects. Farrowing's end-task sheets already do this.

backlog.title: Closed receipt is a stub
backlog.detail: The page says 'Results page not designed yet'. Farrowing has a finished task receipt; the generic one should reuse it.

backlog.title: What does 'Day N of N' mean for tasks with no batch window?
backlog.detail: Pregnancy, Heat and Return-heat windows differ; Nursery and Finishing exits have no definition. Show Day N, a countdown or nothing.
options: Hide the pill when no window
Show 'Day N' only
Invent a default window
backlog.recommendation: Hide the pill when there is no configured window.

backlog.title: Do treatments, vaccinations and transfers get Home cards?
backlog.detail: The Home card study proposes them as the owner's three major operational tasks; the workbench PRD and samples list only production tasks. Nursery and finishing exits are acknowledged but undefined.
options: Add cards for all three
Keep Home to production tasks
Add treatments and vaccinations only
backlog.recommendation: Decide before designing Prescriptions; recommend treatments and vaccinations only, as they have Figma.

backlog.title: Opening Piglet processing from a unit passes a unit the prototype ignores
backlog.detail: unit=6 and returnUnit=6 are forwarded but the prototype shows every pen; Back does not return to the unit.

backlog.title: 'Tomorrow' card in a quiet section is hard-coded
backlog.detail: Growth check, Batch 26 is fixed text, not derived from a task; Growth check has no definition elsewhere.

backlog.title: Home task card lives only in prototype code, not the design system
backlog.detail: The pattern points at one screen and has no component, README or gate; the card is a bespoke JS and CSS renderer beside the Task skeleton's TaskSummary, two different summary cards. Strings are literal, not from the strings file.

backlog.title: Which Breeding states and six search cases are in?
backlog.detail: Old Figma has 8 running, 7 ended screens and six search cases A-F (pig not in batch or unit). Search is a Find-pig concern across tasks, and ended-task reading repeats every task's pattern. Scope it before drawing.
options: Build on the Task skeleton; search handled by shared Find pig
Keep the six search cases inside Breeding
backlog.recommendation: Task skeleton plus shared search; fold the six cases into one Find pig flow.

backlog.title: Is heat check one form shared with the Heat event?
backlog.detail: The task has 13 running and 17 ended screens and a boar-transfer sub-flow; the Heat placeholder records the same event from a pig. The Breeding section says one form, one record from any door.
options: Task rows open the Heat form
Task has its own mark form that writes the same record
backlog.recommendation: Task rows open the Heat form; boar transfer is Move.

backlog.title: Sow check form has no field list
backlog.detail: Figma gives only the initial state of one form; the fields, the outcome and what 'checked' does to the growing denominator are not stated. Needs references before designing.

backlog.title: Weaning check, Wean and Mark as breeder overlap three ways
backlog.detail: The Weaning check task (10+17 screens), the Wean event and Mark as breeder all record weaning, piglet info and breeder choice. Piglet processing already marks breeders. Which is the door and which the form?
options: Task rows open the Wean form; breeders chosen in the Mark as breeder form
Weaning task owns the whole flow including identity
Wean form is pig-only; the task only checks
backlog.recommendation: Task rows open the Wean form; identity stays in Mark as breeder.

backlog.title: No reference beyond the list tab
backlog.detail: Figma holds only the pig list; result options, first and second check, unclear recheck and ended state are not drawn although Home cards already show them.

backlog.title: No reference beyond the list tab
backlog.detail: Figma holds only the list; Home rules say observation has no completion bar and 'no return' is not evidence, but no check form or end flow exists.

backlog.title: What does an end-nursery check record?
backlog.detail: Only a list tab exists; unclear whether it moves pigs, checks weight or just confirms. Overlaps Move and Weight, and has no Home card definition.
options: Confirm and move
Check only
Merge into one end-stage task
backlog.recommendation: Merge with end-finishing into one end-stage task once the owner defines the move.

backlog.title: Is end-finishing the same task as end-nursery?
backlog.detail: Only a list tab exists with no Home card definition; sale or transfer rules are unknown.
options: Same task with a stage setting
Separate task
backlog.recommendation: Same task with a stage setting.

backlog.title: What does Pig list own that Pig profile does not?
backlog.detail: The Figma file holds list, filter, detail, health and events; detail and health are already built as Pig profile and Health record. Only the list, filters, more actions and Edit pig info remain.
options: Pig list is search and filter only, opening Pig profile
Drop the page; use Inspection's list
backlog.recommendation: Search and filter only, opening Pig profile; Edit pig info joins its actions.

backlog.title: Duplicates Health record; keep only the missing parts
backlog.detail: Add, remove or recover and triage are built as Health record (record health, resolve conditions, care instructions). Left over: second confirmations. Mark as duplicate or reduce to the catalogue.

backlog.title: Is triage the same thing as care level?
backlog.detail: Health record has four care levels while the old file has triage levels with confirmations on leaving, recovering or removing. Two names for one idea?
options: One concept, called care
Keep triage as the supervisor term
backlog.recommendation: One concept, called care; retire the triage placeholder.

backlog.title: Per-pig Treat or Prescriptions as the treatment flow?
backlog.detail: Health record already builds Record treatment (medicine, many pigs). Prescriptions is a different, newer plan flow. Treat's 'no disease' state needs a rule.
options: Keep both; the free treatment stays in Health record
Prescription flow only
backlog.recommendation: Keep both; the free treatment stays in Health record and Treat is retired.

backlog.title: How does a prescription relate to per-pig treatment?
backlog.detail: 28 screens in nine groups (2025.9) with scan, skip dose and abnormality states; the largest unbuilt flow. Overlaps Data sync (waiting treatments) and the open Home card question.
options: Prescriptions are plans that create treatment records
Separate record types
backlog.recommendation: Plans that create the same treatment record; decide the Home card first.

backlog.title: Death is drawn in three places
backlog.detail: Farrowing's death sheet, Piglet processing's Record death and this Inspection flow (10 screens) each record death. Which is the shared form and how does it count against batches?
options: One death form with piglet and sow variants
Keep each local
backlog.recommendation: One death form; entry points differ only by preset.

backlog.title: Miscarriage built in Pig profile vs Abortion placeholder
backlog.detail: Pig profile already builds Record miscarriage and Farrowing's outcomes use it; this feature repeats it as three placeholder screens (6 in Figma). Same event, two names.
options: Retire Abortion; miscarriage is the form
Rename the built form to Abortion
backlog.recommendation: Retire Abortion; keep the built Record miscarriage.

backlog.title: Retire Record farrowing in favour of the Farrowing task?
backlog.detail: Farrowing is built with counting, finish and edit. Record farrowing (8 old screens) is the pig-door duplicate, including preconditions and 'join batch'.
options: Pig action opens the Farrowing sheet
Keep as a separate quick form
backlog.recommendation: Pig action opens the Farrowing sheet; keep only join-batch.

backlog.title: Fostering vs Piglet processing 'Move piglets'
backlog.detail: Piglet processing builds Move piglets within a batch; fostering moves between sows and across stages. Is fostering a move, or its own event with parentage?
options: Fostering is Move piglets with a receiving sow
Own event
backlog.recommendation: Fostering is Move piglets with a receiving sow.

backlog.title: Blocked states of the Heat form are not ruled
backlog.detail: The old file draws bred and pregnant pigs as separate states; the section says the sow's state decides what is available, and the form is shared with Heat check.
options: Blocked with the reason
Allow with a warning
backlog.recommendation: Blocked with the reason, as the section text says.

backlog.title: Where is Mark as breeder done?
backlog.detail: Piglet processing marks breeders inline; the Weaning task has 'Keep breeders and fill IDs'; this file has 13 screens plus a No-ID variant. Three doors, three forms.
options: One form, three doors
Only at weaning
backlog.recommendation: One form, three doors.

backlog.title: Line and batch choice repeats Abortion and Heat
backlog.detail: Production line and batch search appear in three events; design the shared line and batch picker once and reuse it.

backlog.title: Wean duplicates the Weaning check task
backlog.detail: The same check and piglet information as the task. The blocked state (farrowing not finished) is a rule shared with Farrowing.
options: Block with the reason
Offer to finish farrowing first
backlog.recommendation: Block with the reason.

backlog.title: One-pig measure already built in Pig profile
backlog.detail: Pig profile's Record weight, temperature or backfat takes one reading per pig; this placeholder duplicates that form.

backlog.title: Weight appears as pig reading, litter weight and task check
backlog.detail: Individual weight, Piglet litter weight and the weaning check each weigh. The old file hides weight in the backfat group.
options: One weight form with a pig or litter target
Keep separate
backlog.recommendation: One weight form with a pig or litter target.

backlog.title: One-pig measure already built in Pig profile
backlog.detail: Same as Backfat: a duplicate of the built reading form; retire or link.

backlog.title: Move vs batch membership and Piglet 'Move piglets'
backlog.detail: Old Move picks a location for many pigs; Pig profile builds batch membership (batch, not place) and Piglet processing moves piglets between pens. Which events are place moves?
options: One Move form for place; batch changes stay separate
Merge with batch membership
backlog.recommendation: One Move form for place; batch changes stay separate.

backlog.title: Single confirm screen; needs reason and effect
backlog.detail: One screen in Figma. No reason, date or batch effect is specified, and blocked pigs are not described.

backlog.title: Sampling section text is 'Not written yet'
backlog.detail: No shared rules for how rooms, sample types (mixed, pig, person, supply, environment) and result states (waiting, negative, positive) relate. The English and Chinese Figma sections differ.

backlog.title: Sync section text is 'Not written yet'
backlog.detail: No shared rules for what syncs, conflict handling or how it relates to Home's Saved work drawer.

backlog.title: Which Figma section is the reference: Chinese or English V2.0?
backlog.detail: The English one is shorter and uses different screens. Sampling also needs an owner and a Home entrance.
options: Chinese
English
Merge
backlog.recommendation: Chinese, the fuller one.

backlog.title: Is Data sync a page or part of the Saved-work drawer?
backlog.detail: 17 old screens (2025.4): entry banner, list, per-pig and per-treatment detail with conflict and empty states, and upload. Home already has a drawer. Treatment sync is tied to Prescriptions.
options: Drawer is the list; detail is a sheet
Separate page
backlog.recommendation: Drawer is the list, detail a sheet.

backlog.title: Adjust feed screen opens the walk list, not the editor
backlog.detail: Bare and in the atlas phone, feed-plan.editor has no preset or steps, so it renders the plain walk. The most important feed screen cannot be reviewed.

backlog.title: End date and note screen opens the walk list
backlog.detail: No preset or steps on this screen, so it renders the unit walk. The date and note form that the notes describe is not shown.

backlog.title: Pig feed plan screen opens the walk list
backlog.detail: No preset or steps; the page that should show the Feeding block and Base curve renders the walk instead.

backlog.title: Boar and piglet rows are off-screen when opened
backlog.detail: The screen should show boars and piglets but opens at the top (C1 sow rows); the B1 and P1 pens sit far below the fold, so its point is not visible.

backlog.title: Hospital-care tag is not in view on the care-levels screen
backlog.detail: The notes point at Diarrhoea on 000801 with Move to hospital pen, but the screen opens at the top; that row is below the fold, so the four care levels are not seen together.

backlog.title: Sow 000306 reads 'Gestation · 40 days' here, '—' on the walk
backlog.detail: The record header shows 40 days, but the walk and pig-profile.empty show 'Gestation · —' (no stage start). Same pig, two stage readings.

backlog.title: Sow 000281 has different age and breed on two health screens
backlog.detail: health-record.ongoing shows 1080 days and breed '—'; health-record.many shows 1280 days and Yorkshire. Same ear tag, conflicting data.

backlog.title: Last outcome card is clipped at the sheet edge
backlog.detail: Recheck later is cut off at the bottom of the outcome list, with its border and radius cropped before the Note field.

backlog.title: Pen header counts and feed total ignore the active filter
backlog.detail: The count '3 pigs' and the kg total cover all pigs while rows show only filtered pigs. The total does not match the rows a worker sees.

backlog.title: Plural not handled: '1 days', '1 days old', '1 days ago'
backlog.detail: An ongoing condition on day 1 reads '1 days'; pig-profile Age and Last service repeat the fault. Needs a plural rule in the copy.

backlog.title: Check-in author and times are fixed text (G. Hansen, 06:40, 09:41)
backlog.detail: 'Last check-in', the walk log and the confirmation use constants, not the signed-in worker and real times. A developer cannot tell what is real.

backlog.title: An open equipment fault has no sign on the list
backlog.detail: The screen should show a pen with a note and a fault, but it renders like the walk: no fault mark exists, and the fault shows only in the pen log after it is reported.

backlog.title: Pen peek has a fault line that is never filled
backlog.detail: The preview carries a fault line in code but nothing feeds it. A pen of unknown feeding mode also reads 'Ad-lib' in the peek feed line.

backlog.title: Finding day count is stored as 1 and never advances
backlog.detail: 'Day N' is the urgency cue on rows and tags, but the prototype never increments it. Seeded findings also show 'Recorded — · —'.

backlog.title: Feed end date passes and nothing returns the pig to the curve
backlog.detail: The end date is a plain date; no rule restores the pig to the base curve when it passes, so the 'until' promise is empty.

backlog.title: Feed amounts show one decimal on rows, two in the editor
backlog.detail: A pig row reads 2.6 kg/day while the editor shows 2.64; the same number reads differently on two screens.

backlog.title: Search, review and scan show 'Gestating'; the row says 'Gestation'
backlog.detail: Find, Selected and Scan sheets use the raw stage word, the walk row uses stage and days. Same pig, two stage strings.

backlog.title: Weight, temperature and backfat accept any value above 0
backlog.detail: No upper bound or normal range; a typo of 1800 kg saves. In bulk, one invalid row blocks the whole save.

backlog.title: After a reading, the sheet drops to the walk, not the pig
backlog.detail: Reading, body condition and note forms return to the walk list; task, miscarriage and batch forms return to the record. One sheet family, two return rules.

backlog.title: Not in pig changes batch and stage with no confirmation or undo
backlog.detail: One tap among three equal choices removes the sow from her batch and sets her Off production / Open. A mis-tap cannot be recovered here.

backlog.title: Draw or delete the unit summary, sensors, batches and fault flows?
backlog.detail: 13 placeholder screens (sensors, batches, unit sheet, pen faults, report, resolve) exist only in code; no control reaches them. The Environment feature already owns sensors, maintenance and report-issue.
options: Delete all 13; Environment owns sensors and faults
Keep a one-line unit summary (pigs, pens, open faults) linking to Environment
Draw the full summary card, batch tracker and fault flow here
backlog.recommendation: Delete the sensor and fault screens (Environment covers them); keep at most a one-line unit summary with a link.

backlog.title: Is the batch tracker part of the walk?
backlog.detail: Batch tracker, batch sheet and batch filter are built but unreachable, and the filter has no field. The ROUND-3 carousel is gone. Tasks already organise work by batch.
options: Remove batch tracker and batch filter from Inspection
Place a batch row on the walk and enable the filter
Show batch only on the pig record
backlog.recommendation: Remove from Inspection; tasks and the pig record already carry batch.

backlog.title: Where does the pen head-count check live?
backlog.detail: The section text promises pen-count checks, but no Inspection screen exists. Research (pen-count.md) designs count correction as a pen-scoped event, with no screen in the atlas.
options: Add a pen count row to the pen sheet
Leave count correction to Fostering and Missing features
Drop the claim from the section text
backlog.recommendation: Add one row to the pen sheet that opens the pen count, so the text matches the product.

backlog.title: Default Care when recording a finding: No action needed or Monitor?
backlog.detail: The shortest path (choose Fever, Save) records a fever as an ongoing non-alert, so it never appears under needs attention.
options: Keep No action needed as default
Default to Monitor for all findings
Make Care a required choice with no default
backlog.recommendation: Make Care a required choice with no default, so a fever cannot silently become a non-alert.

backlog.title: Does 'Move to hospital pen' actually move the pig?
backlog.detail: Hospital pen is a care choice only: no pen change, no task, nothing. The label promises an action the app does not take.
options: Rename to 'Needs hospital pen' (a flag)
Open the Move flow from the care choice
Remove the level
backlog.recommendation: Rename it as a flag and link to Move from the finding, so the app does not imply a move that did not happen.

backlog.title: Should 'Entered in error' need a confirmation?
backlog.detail: Save outcome closes a finding as Entered in error with no second step, and also ends a linked feed adjustment. The log keeps the record but the active one is gone.
options: Keep one tap
Confirm line for Entered in error only
Undo for 10 seconds
backlog.recommendation: Undo for 10 seconds; cheaper than a confirm dialog with gloves.

backlog.title: Where do medicines, brands, methods and units come from?
backlog.detail: The list is a sample ('Antibiotic A', 'Sample brand A'). Farm configuration does not exist. Prescriptions is a separate feature that may supply the medicine.
options: Farm-configured list owned by management web
Fixed global list for the pilot
Prefill from Prescriptions when a task opened the form
backlog.recommendation: Farm-configured list, prefilled from Prescriptions when a task opened the form.

backlog.title: Which feed fields show, and on which page?
backlog.detail: ASTRA-FEED-PLAN-FIELDS proposes brand, supplier, energy, protein and lysine; none is drawn, and protein and lysine units are unconfirmed. Pen page, pig page or neither?
options: Pen page only: formula, brand, nutrition
Pig page only
Neither; keep formula, mode and kg
backlog.recommendation: Pen page: formula and brand only; nutrition values stay in the management web.

backlog.title: Does saving a feed change drop a body-condition link silently?
backlog.detail: Save ends the link between a Thin finding and its feed adjustment; Resolve warns but the editor does not. Body condition says 'Feed stays unchanged', so the link may be dead product.
options: Keep the link and warn on the editor
Drop linking entirely (body condition records only)
Link and end the finding too
backlog.recommendation: Drop linking entirely; delete the link copy on the finding and resolve screens.

backlog.title: One way back to the curve: mode, 0% or Reset?
backlog.detail: Follow curve, percent 0 and Reset all return to the curve. Three controls for one outcome add taps and confusion.
options: Keep Follow curve only
Keep Reset only
Keep all three
backlog.recommendation: Keep the Follow curve mode; remove Reset and treat 0% as the same state.

backlog.title: Should 'Hold amount' show kg and an end?
backlog.detail: The tag reads 'Feed held' with kg only in a tooltip; a gloved worker cannot see how much or until when. Hold also freezes the curve until reset.
options: Show 'Held 2.6 kg' on the tag
Keep tooltip; show on the pig page only
Remove Hold; use percent only
backlog.recommendation: Show 'Held 2.6 kg' on the tag, with no tooltip dependence.

backlog.title: Show a pen-wide feed change at the pen, not on every pig?
backlog.detail: A pen-wide +10% repeats as a tag on every row; the pen header shows only the new kg.
options: Tag once on the pen header; pig rows show only individual changes
Keep a tag per pig
Both
backlog.recommendation: Tag once on the pen header; show pig tags only for individual changes.

backlog.title: Hide or disable Adjust feed on ad-lib pens?
backlog.detail: Adjust feed is offered and always answers 'unavailable': a dead end on the main bottom button.
options: Hide the button
Show it disabled with the reason
Keep
backlog.recommendation: Hide the button; the page already says Ad-lib.

backlog.title: What do the 'Health' and 'Feed' counts count?
backlog.detail: Health counts any condition, ongoing included; Feed mixes pigs with a change and every pig in a pen whose formula is due. A worker reads both as 'pigs to check'.
options: Health = needs attention only; Feed = pigs with an individual change
Rename the lenses
Keep, add a one-line legend
backlog.recommendation: Count needs-attention pigs only; show formula-due at the pen header, not as pigs.

backlog.title: Should check-in require anything?
backlog.detail: Check-in is allowed with nothing recorded and pens unseen. Is a unit walk a fact the farm can rely on?
options: Allow always
Warn when pens are unvisited
Require every pen opened
backlog.recommendation: Warn with the unseen-pen count; do not block.

backlog.title: Show the care level as words on the row?
backlog.detail: Monitor, Treat in place and Move to hospital pen differ only by icon and colour; the words are in a tooltip. A gloved worker cannot tell them apart.
options: Words on every tag
Words on needs-attention tags only
Distinct icon shape
backlog.recommendation: Put the care word on needs-attention tags; ongoing keeps the neutral tag.

backlog.title: Edit and Close note overlap: keep one note per pen?
backlog.detail: Edit overwrites the author; Close archives to the log. Two actions on one note, and the first writer disappears from the card.
options: One note; edit keeps the original author line
Allow several notes
Keep
backlog.recommendation: Keep one note; show 'edited by' while keeping the first author.

backlog.title: One pig note that replaces the old one, or a list?
backlog.detail: A new note overwrites the previous one and the sheet does not say so; the log keeps both.
options: Keep one note; say it replaces
Short list of notes
Notes only in the log
backlog.recommendation: Notes only in the log; remove the overwrite.

backlog.title: What order and content for the pig record?
backlog.detail: Six blocks, with Batch, stage, Next task and Type repeated; a sow's age is in days; empty rows draw '—'. A worker at the pen needs care and next action first.
options: Attention, tasks, feeding, then a collapsed Details
Keep six blocks and hide empty rows
Tabs: Now, Facts, History
backlog.recommendation: Attention, tasks and feeding first; facts collapsed; hide empty rows; age in months for sows.

backlog.title: Draw lifetime figures or keep batch history only?
backlog.detail: Litters, born total, farrowing and weaning rates, interval and non-productive days are seeded but not drawn. Do supervisors need them on the phone?
options: Draw the main four on Production stats
Leave to the management web
Remove the seeded data
backlog.recommendation: Leave to the management web.

backlog.title: Can ear tag or breed be corrected from Origin?
backlog.detail: The page is read-only; a wrong ear tag or breed cannot be fixed. A mistaken tag is a common farm error.
options: Read-only on the phone
Edit for breed and tag with a log entry
Fix from the Pig list
backlog.recommendation: Read-only on the phone; corrections in the management web.

backlog.title: One door per finding: merge Edit, Resolve and Care instructions?
backlog.detail: Three bulk rows plus Edit finding and Resolve or remove change the same finding. Names clash: 'Resolve conditions' and 'Resolve or remove'.
options: One 'Update conditions' row with care and outcome together
Keep rows, rename them in line
Bulk only through selected pigs
backlog.recommendation: One row 'Update conditions' for one or many pigs, with care and outcome in one form.

backlog.title: Where do tasks live: card, Next task row, or Actions?
backlog.detail: The same task shows as a card on the record, as Next task and as a row in Actions with a cluster heading that repeats its name.
options: Cards on the record only; Actions opens the task
Actions only
Keep
backlog.recommendation: Cards on the record only; remove task rows from Actions.

backlog.title: Should Move pig overwrite her stage, and say so?
backlog.detail: Moving a pig sets her stage to the new batch's stage, which the form does not state.
options: Keep, and state it on the form
Do not change stage
Ask which
backlog.recommendation: Keep the rule and state it above the Save button.

backlog.title: Miscarriage reason: free text or evidence choices?
backlog.detail: Miscarriage takes free text while 'Not in pig' offers evidence choices; two forms for a similar loss, and no check for an outcome already recorded.
options: Same choices on both
Merge into one outcome form
Keep
backlog.recommendation: Merge into one 'Pregnancy ended' form with choices and optional text.

backlog.title: Drop the Health / General tabs in the action sheet?
backlog.detail: Two small groups sit in one scroll with footer tabs. Tabs add taps for a few rows.
options: Remove the tabs
Keep
Section headings only
backlog.recommendation: Remove the tabs.

backlog.title: Does Health own death and triage, or only conditions?
backlog.detail: Section text lists conditions, triage, deaths and treatments. Care replaced triage; deaths and prescriptions are separate features. Which belong in this section's contract?
options: Findings, care and treatment only
Include death and prescriptions
Rename the section
backlog.recommendation: Findings, care and treatment only; deaths and prescriptions get their own sections.

backlog.title: Catalogue is three levels deep with no recent list
backlog.detail: Tab, door, then item before a fever is chosen. A frequent condition sits two doors deep each time.

backlog.title: Two near-identical pickers: Choose conditions and Link condition
backlog.detail: Same catalogue with another layout for treatment. Gloved workers need one picker with a recent and common list on top.

backlog.title: Four rows for one finding; Edit and Resolve both change it
backlog.detail: Edit finding, Record treatment, Resolve or remove and Review feed adjustment compete. Needs one primary action and a clear secondary.

backlog.title: Care instructions and Edit conditions are one form under two titles
backlog.detail: Same screen, different log entry ('Triage updated' vs 'Finding edited'); the second title adds no function.

backlog.title: 'Health' means three things on one screen
backlog.detail: It labels every attention row, the Health field in details and the Actions group. Duration is 'Day 2' for attention and '120 days' for ongoing.

backlog.title: Temperature 39.5 is unflagged beside a Fever finding
backlog.detail: The reading sits in General details, far from the Fever row, and nothing marks it high. No sign whether treatment was given for Fever.

backlog.title: Sideways scrolling hides the oldest ongoing conditions
backlog.detail: Lameness and Coughing are cut off in a scrolling row; the longest-running conditions are the least visible.

backlog.title: Care level differs only by icon and colour
backlog.detail: Four levels use small icons and colour; colour-blind workers and text-only readers cannot tell them apart.

backlog.title: Dose is 'per pig' in one place and 'for all' in another
backlog.detail: Dose labels differ between single and bulk; treatment from a finding and from the Health group differ only by a fixed condition.

backlog.title: Log wording differs: 'Record corrected' vs 'Finding entered in error'
backlog.detail: Bulk and single forms log the same outcome with two phrases. One wording per outcome.

backlog.title: Save reads 'Save · 0 pigs' while disabled
backlog.detail: A disabled button should say Save, not a count of zero.

backlog.title: Start date and author cannot be corrected on a finding
backlog.detail: Seeded findings show 'Recorded — · —'. The edit form changes name, care and note, never the start.

backlog.title: Two doors to a pen's feed; the note shows twice
backlog.detail: The pen header opens the editor, the Feed guidance row opens the reading page first. The note sits in a card, an Edit row and the pen log.

backlog.title: Filter state has batch, health status and manual feed, but no controls
backlog.detail: Three filters exist in state and the strip label but cannot be set. The Health lens and condition/care filters overlap.

backlog.title: Scan and Search open almost the same sheet; no ear-notch search
backlog.detail: The identity notes list ear-notch search, absent here. Camera scanning is a stub with a sample-tag button. Untagged groups cannot be found.

backlog.title: Three names for one thing: Log, Updates this walk, This walk
backlog.detail: Button, aria label and sheet title differ, and the same events repeat in each pig log and the pen log.

backlog.title: Two Back controls do the same thing
backlog.detail: The header Back and 'Back to unit' on the confirmation both return to the unit.

backlog.title: Log category is inferred from titles for old entries
backlog.detail: A renamed title silently falls into Notes. The same log and filter bar is shared with the pig log.

backlog.title: Long-press peek is hard with gloves; 'N health' misreads as pigs
backlog.detail: Hold 350 ms is hard with gloves and not discoverable. '2 health' counts ongoing conditions, not pigs needing care.

backlog.title: Selected sheet shows raw stage 'Gestating'
backlog.detail: The row repeats 'Gestating' where the list says 'Gestation · 40 days', and has no pen context for the pig.

backlog.title: Sheet header says only '2 pigs' and names nobody
backlog.detail: The worker cannot confirm who the action applies to. Body condition also sits under Measurements though it creates a health finding.

backlog.title: Row clock and record clock disagree
backlog.detail: Row: 'Gestation · 40 days' (days in stage); record: 'Last service · 40 days ago'. Two clocks that can differ; the screen duplicates the walk with one row changed.

backlog.title: Check-in sheet shows a large zero when nothing was recorded
backlog.detail: 'Recorded during this walk 0' dominates; the empty state could say so in words.

backlog.title: 'Formula due' on the walk has no explanation here
backlog.detail: Nothing tells the worker what formula change is due or when; the page shows only formula, mode and kg.

backlog.title: Editor carries mode, percent, slider, chips and a table for one decision
backlog.detail: Too much for gloved hands on one sheet; a pen-total preview exists in code and is not drawn. The scope reads '3 pigs' without naming the pen.

backlog.title: 'Feed for these pigs' sits under a tab called Pens
backlog.detail: Pens and pigs mean the same row. No row reaches equipment faults though a pen chooser exists in the code.

backlog.title: Pig feed page cannot adjust and repeats the record's block
backlog.detail: The only change path is the Actions sheet; the Feeding block is identical on the record. The curve source name is not drawn.

backlog.title: A decrease uses the same neutral tag as an increase
backlog.detail: Direction is only the sign; nothing distinguishes a drop in feed visually.

backlog.title: Four dashes in a row read as a broken page
